sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Biocompatible Dental Ceramic Blocks and Milling Discs

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Mixed Legal System): Civil law governs private-law matters under the Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991); public-law, criminal-law, and federal corporate-governance matters follow the common-law tradition; federal statutes and regulations apply uniformly across Canada and prevail over provincial law in case of conflict.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA)
Convention Between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (US-Canada Tax Treaty, including the 2023 amending Protocol)
Convention Between Canada and France for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (Canada-France Tax Treaty)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended, and its Regulations (SOR/2002-184 et seq.); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 462.3 et seq.; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, and associated Regulations; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 13; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act), SC 2017, c 21; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 51.1 (register of individuals with significant control); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1; Act respecting the transparency of the enterprise, CQLR c E-25.1 (Quebec ultimate beneficial owner declaration regime); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; FINTRAC guidance and interpretations on beneficial ownership, politically exposed persons, and sanctions screening under the PCMLTFA.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence / Status (Certificat de conformité) of the ultimate parent or foreign incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent authority of the jurisdiction of origin (e.g., the Secretary of State for a US parent entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents); consular legalization where the origin country is not a Hague-member state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Procuration) appointing the Quebec incorporator and registered representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized statutory declarations of identity, residence, and good standing for each proposed director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of the apostilled corporate and identity documents (required under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator enrolled with the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec (OTTIAQ)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translation certification by the OTTIAQ-certified translator; the underlying apostilled original must be attached

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for the initial paid-in capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution holding the incorporation funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille (where the issuing bank is located in a Hague-member state)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, initial shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, and the Canadian sanctions regulations adopted under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the United Nations Act, the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act); enhanced due-diligence measures apply to any politically exposed person (PEP), including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates, in line with FINTRAC regulations and the PCMLTFA; a risk-based review of the source of funds for the initial share subscription is mandatory; any positive hit must be escalated to counsel for a frozen-assets and legal-restriction assessment before any filing with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Centre de services électroniques (online filing and name-reservation portal at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), the corporate name must be drafted in French; a French version and an English version may both be recorded, with the French version prevailing in all legal publicity; names must use Latin script, including French diacritics; the legal-element suffix must be one of 'Société par actions', 'Incorporée', 'Corporation', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'S.A.'; a purely foreign-language name requires an accompanying French version for registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chartered Professional Accountant / Comptable professionnel agréé

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, ss 11-14, 21, 26, 46 and 67; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss 2, 11-13; alternative federal regime: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 7-9
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) - Online CLIC Portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (Articles constitutifs) followed by initial Declaration of Registration (Declaration d'immatriculation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account required under QBCA; the board fixes the consideration for issued shares, provided that at least one class of shares carries unrestricted voting rights and at least one class entitles holders to remaining property on dissolution (QBCA s 11(2))
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the first board meeting of [Company] held at the registered office in Quebec: First, the incorporators' subscription to 100,000 common shares is accepted, and the Board authorizes issuance upon receipt of full consideration. Second, the registered office is established at [street], City of [city], Province of Quebec; the corporate seal, minute book, and statutory registers are adopted. Third, the following officers are appointed: [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each with operating authority under the Board's direction. Fourth, management is instructed to complete all statutory registrations and regulatory license filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name search and reservation via NUANS report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Name Search and NUANS online service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed corporate name, verify the name is distinct and not prohibited under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, and reserve the approved name for a period of 90 days. The French-language version of the name must be declared as the legal name or a bilingual version must be filed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as not distinct, modify the distinctive element or obtain a written consent or waiver from the holder of the conflicting name under P-44.1 s 19, then resubmit the NUANS request within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of articles of incorporation and issuance of certificate of constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - CLIC online incorporation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation in accordance with QBCA s 12 including corporate name, registered office address, authorized share capital, any restrictions on share transfers, number of directors, and standard clauses. File the executed articles electronically via CLIC, pay the official filing fee of CAD 200, and receive the certificate of constitution issued under QBCA s 26. The company acquires legal personality upon issuance of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Consent to act of each director
Proof of registered office address (lease or attestation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an objection letter, correct the stated deficiencies, refile the articles with the revised text, and pay the applicable fee; a contested refusal may be appealed by way of judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal publicity declaration and issuance of Quebec enterprise number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Declaration d'immatriculation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days after the certificate of constitution, file the initial Declaration of Registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises disclosing the corporate name, jurisdiction, registered office, directors, and primary business activity. Pay the CAD 38 registration fee and obtain the NEQ (numero d'entreprise du Quebec), which is the mandatory identifier for all provincial government dealings.
required_dossiers: Complete list of directors with residential addresses
Identity of the person responsible for the enterprise
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected or queried, correct the particulars online through CLIC within the notice period and request rectification; late-filing penalties may be cancelled upon demonstration of reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of first board resolution, by-laws, and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office and corporate secretary - intra-corporate statutory function under QBCA ss 46 and 67
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational board meeting, adopt the first board resolution approving the incorporation and share issuance, fix the registered office by instrument under QBCA s 21, adopt by-laws governing the conduct of affairs, appoint officers, approve the corporate seal and minute book, and open the register of directors, register of shareholders, and records of resolutions in accordance with QBCA s 67.
required_dossiers: Share subscription list and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a procedural omission is discovered, adopt a curative board resolution or a memorandum of correction and complete the statutory registers promptly before the fiscal year-end to avoid penalties under QBCA ss 67-72.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and provincial statutory registrations for Business Number, QST, and CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; Revenu Quebec; Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online with CRA for the nine-digit Business Number (BN) and register for GST/HST, payroll deductions, and corporate income tax accounts. Simultaneously open a file with Revenu Quebec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and employer source deductions, and register with CNESST as an employer for occupational health and safety coverage. Confirm whether the 1% workforce skills development contribution applies once payroll thresholds are met.
required_dossiers: Estimated GST/HST sales and registration date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is blocked, contact CRA Business Enquiries at 1-800-959-5525 or the Revenu Quebec account helpline, correct identity documentation, and request a new access code; retroactive registration is available where an account was opened late.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada - Medical Devices Directorate (federal) and Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE), Quebec - Manufacturing and Product Licensing Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282, ss 44-45, together with municipal industrial occupancy permit (certificat d'occupation) issued under the Quebec Construction Code, Chapter I

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP); Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (federal)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III - Declaration of Compliance under the Regulation respecting the declaration, authorization and registration of certain activities (RRDEAE), applicable to dental-ceramic block machining and sintering installations under 1 MW thermal capacity; no federal EIA designation under Impact Assessment Act Schedule 1 (Exempt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Air emissions: particulate matter below 50 mg/m3 stack threshold per Quebec Air Contaminants Regulation (Q-2, r 4.1) and municipal by-law limits; Wastewater discharge to municipal sewer: pH 6.0-9.5, BOD5 no greater than 500 mg/L, total suspended solids no greater than 600 mg/L; Solid waste: zirconia dust and rejected blocks managed as non-hazardous industrial waste, or routed through authorized hazardous waste carriers when contaminated with machining fluids.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (attestation de conformite incendie) from the local fire safety service under the Fire Safety Act, CQLR c S-3.4; structural and occupancy clearance from the municipal permit office under the Quebec Construction Code, Chapter I; CNESST workplace health and safety clearance covering occupational exposure to zirconia dust, heat, and noise, including annual air monitoring and audiometric testing plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via Business Registration Online (BRO); in Quebec, additionally Revenu Québec (RQ) through the Registraire des entreprises / Services Québec portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign corporation obtains a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online using either a Canadian-based director or a certified agent under the Excise Tax Act and Income Tax Act; concurrently registers with Revenu Québec for QST and provincial payroll accounts via the province's enterprise registration system; non-resident corporations carrying on business in Quebec may have simplified QST registration but remain subject to federal Part I filing obligations
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — Canadian corporate income tax under Part I of the Income Tax Act; no pass-through eligibility for a business corporation; non-resident shareholders subject to Canadian branch tax and withholding regimes; no territorial classification for active business income earned in Canada
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; available statutory elections include section 85 rollover, section 219 deemed-residence election, section 216(4) rental income election, functional currency election under section 261, GST/QST quick-method and streamlined-rebate elections, and hybrid-mismatch limitation rules under ITA sections 18.2 and 18.3 (Budget 2021 implementation)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) combined with Quebec QST (provincial value-added-style consumption tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 gross worldwide taxable supplies in the preceding four trailing calendar quarters; once exceeded, GST/HST and QST registration become mandatory
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing obligation is currently in force; CRA and Revenu Québec accept conventional paper/PDF and optional PEPPOL-compliant e-invoices; electronic issuance is permissible but the issuer must preserve an auditable chronological set of data and source documents for six years

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of dental zirconia blocks exported by the manufacturer qualify for zero-rating under ETA Schedule VI Part V (section 1) and corresponding Quebec QST zero-rating provisions; the exporter must establish that title and risk of loss passed to a non-resident purchaser and that the goods were physically delivered from Canada via an export transaction; closely related services directly invoiced with the export goods are also eligible
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Commercial Invoice and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) cargo-control documentation
Export Declaration (B13A / CAED; or ACI eManifest filing where applicable)
Bill of Lading or sea/air waybill evidencing departure from Canada
certified freight-forwarder or customs-broker certificate of export
Inward remittance / SWIFT-wire or TT transfer records as proof of consideration in settlement of the sale
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation ceiling for exporters; nevertheless, CRA and Revenu Québec retain a six-year audit look-back under which any export zero-rating claim lacking documentary substantiation will be reversed, resulting in reassessed GST/QST, daily compounding interest under ETA section 280.1 and QST equivalent provisions, penalty equal to 50% of the grossed-up understated tax under ITA section 163(2) / ETA section 280, additional Revenu Québec negligence penalties, and possible civil fraud prosecution under the Criminal Code for intentional misrepresentation

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a free current account convertibility regime under IMF Article VIII, permitting unrestricted repatriation of export proceeds, royalty payments, and profit remittances for manufacturing corporations. Capital account transactions remain subject to prior review by Finance Canada or OSFI for investments exceeding CAD 100 million or involving certain real estate or portfolio securities. Quebec-based dental ceramic manufacturers face no material convertibility barriers for core trade settlements or intercompany funding when supported by verifiable commercial documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation exists for export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency in offshore or domestic foreign currency accounts and convert to CAD at prevailing market rates via authorized dealers. All transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported electronically through the Canada Border Services Agency Customs and Trade Online (CBSA CTOL) system. Profit remittances to foreign parents require supporting documentation for Income Tax Act compliance but are not subject to mandatory conversion ratios.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for regulated fintech platforms including Wise Business and Mercury for cross-border payables and receivables. Legal constraints arise from FINTRAC registration requirements for money services businesses and Quebec provincial AML rules limiting offshore digital EMIs. Corporate clients must maintain full audit trails and may encounter onboarding delays or transaction caps for volumes exceeding CAD 500,000 monthly without correspondent banking relationships.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Schedule 1 Canadian banks permit remote corporate account opening for established entities provided corporate minute books, articles of incorporation, and director KYC questionnaires are submitted. However, Quebec jurisdiction mandates virtual or in-person interviews for directors and authorized signers during initial onboarding to satisfy provincial AML obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from provincial corporate registry, shareholder register, and ultimate beneficial owner declarations certified under PCMLTFA
Quebec business license, NAICS/ISIC registration, export sales contracts, supplier due diligence reports, and product certification documentation
Foreign parent incorporation documents, share subscription agreements, and source-of-funds evidence for capital injections

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from foreign shareholders are processed via SWIFT wire transfers using purpose code 880 or 881 (Capital Contribution). Verification requires board resolution, share issuance documentation, and proof of funds source. All wires must reference the exact legal name and account number of the Quebec corporation. Quebec Revenue Agency and CRA reporting applies for tax residency purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 messages with purpose codes 100 (Trade Payment) or 103 (Commercial Invoice Payment). Larger disbursements employ Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. All payments require matching against underlying purchase orders, invoices, and shipping documents for AML screening and transfer pricing compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for emerging market exposures
Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity management
Options on foreign exchange for asymmetric risk protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec annual declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the registration anniversary date of the legal person; any registrable change, including a share transfer affecting control or beneficial ownership, must be filed as an updating declaration within 30 calendar days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest; repeated failure to file permits the Registraire to issue a notice of administrative dissolution/strike-off, after which the corporation may not carry on business and directors may remain liable for outstanding obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA annual return (where the corporation is federally incorporated or is a CBCA extra-provincial corporation carrying on business in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation; the return confirms the corporation is in good standing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative dissolution risk if the annual return remains unfiled or unpaid for at least two consecutive years; directors and shareholders may be exposed to continued liability after dissolution until restoration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the filing due date is June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month of delinquency for up to 12 months, with no penalty less than CAD 100; compound interest accrues daily on unpaid balances, and director liability may arise for unreported taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return (Quebec provincial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; provincial tax balances and instalment obligations follow Revenu Québec prescribed schedule rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid provincial tax plus an additional 1% per full month for up to 12 months; interest charges accrue on arrears; directors may be liable for unremitted corporate source deductions or tax amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Auditor appointment is mandatory for distributing corporations or corporations whose securities are publicly traded. A private Quebec business corporation may waive the annual independent audit by unanimous shareholder resolution at each financial year-end; there is no prescribed revenue or asset threshold in the QBCA for mandatory audit of a non-distributing corporation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for public/distributing corporations and reporting issuers; private corporations may elect to use Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook – Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Financial statements must be consolidated or prepared according to the chosen framework and presented to shareholders at the annual meeting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual declaration, the corporation must confirm that the recorded shareholders, directors, officers, and individuals with significant control are current and complete. Any share transfer that changes members or beneficial ownership must be recorded in the register of members and reported to the Registraire des entreprises as an updating declaration within 30 days of the event. The individuals-with-significant-control register must be reviewed annually at the general meeting and corrected immediately if material changes are identified.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO/ISC register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 to USD 750 per year for a professional Quebec registered office or registered agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 to USD 9,500 per year for a private dental consumables manufacturing corporation; the expense is nil in years where the unanimous audit waiver is in effect

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Manufacturing and processing tax credit (federal 13% on eligible profits), SR&ED investment tax credit (up to 35% refundable for CCPC, 15% non-refundable for others), Quebec innovation tax credits, and small business deduction for CCPC (not applicable if foreign-controlled).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) – filed via CRA's e-file (NETFILE) or paper
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30 of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net of deductions and adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must file T2; report Canadian-source income only.
Apply treaty provisions if applicable; attach Form T2209 for foreign tax credits.
Allocate income to Quebec using permanent establishment rules; file separate CO-17.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on late payments at prescribed rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return (Quebec) – filed via Revenu Québec's e-filing system (clic Revenu)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 6 months after fiscal year-end (same as federal)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a permanent establishment in Quebec must file; report Quebec-source income.
Claim treaty relief if applicable; attach Form CO-1029 for tax credits.
Only claim credits for activities performed in Quebec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on late payments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must provide a Certificate of Residence (Form NR116) to the payer before the payment. The payer must withhold at the treaty rate if the certificate is provided; otherwise, the statutory 25% applies. For Canada-US treaty, dividends to a US corporation with ≥10% ownership are subject to 5% withholding; other cases 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, reduced to 10% under many treaties (e.g., Canada-US, Canada-UK). Interest: statutory 25%, often reduced to 0% or 10% under treaties (e.g., Canada-US 0% for arm's length, 15% for non-arm's length).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for goods, CAD 500,000 for services, CAD 500,000 for intangibles (per transaction or aggregate); Master File required for transactions exceeding CAD 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like offshore jurisdictions, but applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and requires economic substance for treaty benefits. A corporation must have real business operations, employees, and assets in Canada to claim treaty relief and avoid reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, misrepresentation in tax returns, or failure to file returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fine up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties: 100% of tax amount plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they fail to withhold or remit; travel bans and asset freezes possible under criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without economic substance, solely to avoid tax, launder money, or obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess and deny treaty benefits; penalties up to 50% of tax avoided; potential criminal charges for fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for civil restitution and criminal fines; personal assets may be seized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to report suspicious transactions or large cash transactions under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal penalties for individuals including fines and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be fined and imprisoned; personal liability for non-compliance with AML obligations.
